sections.title: What it is for
body: Estimates how likely a new claim is to be large or complex, so simple claims can be fast-tracked and the rest go straight to an adjuster.
Runs once, when the call ends. A person can change the route with a reason at any time.

sections.title: What it is not for
body: Deciding whether a claim is covered or how much is paid.
Pricing a policy, or judging the caller.

sections.title: What it never looks at
body: No voice stress, accent, speech-rate or pitch features: unreliable and discriminatory.
Proxy for protected characteristics; region-level effects are tested for, not learned.
Age is used only to form age bands for fairness testing.
Identity is not evidence.
The caller's language is tested for fairness, never used to route.
Where the caller lives is tested for fairness, never used to route.

sections.title: How it was tested
body: On 0.89 AUC terms it separates large from small claims well; at the setting in use it sends 91 in 100 of large or complex claims to an adjuster.
Its scores are calibrated: when it says 30 in 100, about 30 in 100 such claims turn out large (expected calibration error 0.012).
It beats a simple scorecard on the same data (PR-AUC 0.77 against 0.72).

sections.title: Fairness
body: The fast-track rate is 40 in 100 overall. Every region, language and age band stays within 5.0 points of it (largest gap 3.5 points, Québec).
Age, language and region are never used to route a claim. We use them only here, to check fairness.

sections.title: Limits
body: It learned from synthetic claim calls shaped like the ones the line takes, with real claim costs from French motor insurance data (freMTPL2). Its absolute accuracy describes that data, not a real book of business; what carries over is the method: calibration, reasons, fairness tests, monitoring and sign-off.
It only knows what the caller said and what the policy shows. Photos and an adjuster's visit come later.

sections.title: Sign-offs
body: A version goes into use only when every gate passes and two different people sign: a claims supervisor and compliance (model risk).

sections.title: For the technical reviewer
body: Algorithm: Gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost), tuned with Optuna; isotonic calibration on the validation months.
Split: Time split: trained on losses before 1 July 2025, calibrated on July to September, tested on October to December 2025.
Test: AUC 0.887, PR-AUC 0.766, Brier 0.0921, ECE 0.0119.
Logistic baseline: AUC 0.849, PR-AUC 0.720; random forest: AUC 0.870, PR-AUC 0.750.
Before calibration: Brier 0.0916, ECE 0.0178; Platt scaling: Brier 0.0918, ECE 0.0168.
Reasons: exact TreeSHAP values; top-5 overlap across 5 bootstrap refits 1.00 (Jaccard).

Public benchmark on freMTPL2 alone (top tenth of claim cost from policy fields): logistic AUC 0.61, XGBoost AUC 0.62. Real French motor claims, policy fields only (no driver age, no region). Whether a claim lands in the top tenth of cost is only weakly predictable from the policy alone; the size of a loss depends on what happened, which is why the size check is trained on what the caller tells the line.

sections.title: What it is for
body: Asks someone in special investigations to look at a claim when several documented signs line up.
A referral is a request for review. It is not a finding of fraud and never denies a claim.

sections.title: What it is not for
body: Denying, delaying or reducing a claim.
Judging a person by who they are: it never sees age, language, region or anything about their voice.

sections.title: How it was tested
body: It refers 4 in 100 claims for review and needs at least two signs before it can refer one.
Of the claims it refers, 48 in 100 turn out to need a closer look in testing; it finds 43 in 100 of those that do.
It beats a simple scorecard on the same data (PR-AUC 0.39 against 0.22); scores are calibrated (expected calibration error 0.007).

sections.title: Fairness
body: The closer-look rate is 4 in 100 overall. Every region, language and age band stays within 1.5 points of it (largest gap 0.3 points, 65 and over).
Age, language and region are never used to route a claim. We use them only here, to check fairness.

sections.title: Limits
body: It learned from synthetic claim calls shaped like the ones the line takes, with real claim costs from French motor insurance data (freMTPL2). Its absolute accuracy describes that data, not a real book of business; what carries over is the method: calibration, reasons, fairness tests, monitoring and sign-off.
It only knows what the caller said and what the policy shows. Photos and an adjuster's visit come later.
The closer-look labels come from documented patterns injected into the synthetic data, with 3 in 100 labels flipped to mimic investigators disagreeing.
